cues.text: A mum who worked so hard
Marcus Rashford was born in 1997 in Manchester, England.
He was the youngest of five children.
His mum, Melanie, brought them up on her own, and she worked more than one job to pay for everything.
Money was very tight.
Sometimes his mum skipped her own meals, so that her children had enough to eat.
Lift the plate cover.
Marcus later said that, all through his childhood, his mum was the leader of the family.
Notice the people who look after you, and thank them. Their love is a kind of strength.
No way to get to training
Marcus started playing at Fletcher Moss Rangers when he was five, first as a goalkeeper.
At seven, he joined the Manchester United academy.
His big brothers helped him choose.
But there was a problem.
His mum and brothers were at work, so often nobody could take him, and he missed training.
Drive the car to training.
His youth coaches, Dave Bushell, Eamon Mulvey and Tony Whelan, found drivers to take him there.
If something is stopping you, tell someone. Asking for help is brave, and people often want to help.
Meals for hungry children
In March 2020, Britain went into lockdown because of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Many children usually got a free lunch at school, called free school meals.
Now, they were missing out.
Marcus remembered where he came from.
He teamed up with a charity called FareShare to get food to children who needed it.
Fill the three food boxes.
People gave over £20 million, and by June the charity had given out 3 million meals across the country.
Remember where you came from. When you know how something feels, you can help others who feel it.
A letter to the government
On 15 June 2020, Marcus wrote an open letter to the government.
He asked them to help end child poverty, which means children growing up without enough money for the things they need.
Just one day later, the government changed its plan, and children kept getting free meals over the summer holidays.
Post the letter.
Marcus said he was proud of helping 1.3 million children.
Later, FareShare named its new warehouse after his mum.
Your voice matters. Speaking up clearly and kindly can help change things for other people.
The penalty that hit the post
In July 2021, England played Italy in the final of Euro 2020.
Marcus came on near the end of extra time.
In the penalty shoot-out, he took England’s third penalty, but it hit the post, and Italy won.
Flip the scoreboard.
Afterwards, some people sent him racist messages online.
Racism means being unfair to someone because of the colour of their skin.
A mural of Marcus in Withington, where he had lived as a boy, was damaged.
A miss does not make you a failure. Racism is never okay: if you see it, tell a grown-up you trust.
A wall of hearts
Then something wonderful happened.
People from the neighbourhood covered the wall with hearts and kind messages for Marcus.
The artist, Akse, came back and painted the mural as good as new.
Put the three hearts on the wall.
Marcus had a tough year and a half after that.
But he kept going, and at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, he scored three goals for England: one against Iran, just after coming on, and two against Wales.
When someone is unkind, kindness can answer back. And you are always more than one result.
